lead: Two random variables often travel together. One observation gives a pair (X, Y), a point on the plane. A joint distribution assigns a probability to every region of that plane. For a fair die rolled twice, X can count 1s and Y can count 2s. For a phone, X can be download time and Y upload time. The joint pmf, joint pdf or joint CDF lets you compute P((X, Y) ∈ A), not only P(X ≤ x) or P(Y ≤ y). This is the base for marginals and independence.
prereq: You need Unit 2: random variables, pmf, pdf, CDF and expectation.

sections.h3: Joint pmf, joint pdf and support

blocks.text: For two discrete random variables X and Y, the joint pmf is p(x,y)=P(X=x,Y=y). It gives the probability of the single pair (x,y). Two rules hold: p(x,y) ≥ 0 for all pairs, and Σ_x Σ_y p(x,y)=1, where both sums run over all possible values. The support is the set of pairs with p(x,y)>0.

For continuous X and Y, the joint pdf f(x,y) is a density, not a probability. A region A gets probability by a double integral: P((X,Y)∈A)=∬_A f(x,y) dx dy. Also f(x,y) ≥ 0 and ∬_{R²} f(x,y) dx dy = 1. A single point has probability 0. A line segment also has probability 0 when the density is finite.

A rectangle [a,b] × [c,d] uses x from a to b and y from c to d. A triangle uses bounds taken from its picture. For example, over 0≤y≤x≤1, the inner y-limit is 0 to x and the outer x-limit is 0 to 1. Do not replace the triangle by the full square 0≤x≤1, 0≤y≤1.

blocks.where: f(x,y) is the joint pdf; A is a region in the plane; dx dy shows integration over x and y.

blocks.text: The joint CDF is F(x,y)=P(X≤x, Y≤y). For discrete variables, F(x,y)=Σ_{u≤x} Σ_{v≤y} p(u,v). For continuous variables, F(x,y)=∫_{-∞}^{x} ∫_{-∞}^{y} f(u,v) dv du. It is non-decreasing in each argument, right-continuous in each, and tends to 0 at either -∞ and to 1 at (+∞,+∞).

A rectangle probability comes from four CDF values. For a<b and c<d, P(a<X≤b, c<Y≤d)=F(b,d)-F(a,d)-F(b,c)+F(a,c). The two negative terms remove strips, and the last term adds back the corner removed twice.
P(a<X≤b, c<Y≤d) = F(b,d) - F(a,d) - F(b,c) + F(a,c)
blocks.where: F is the joint CDF; a,b,c,d are fixed numbers with a<b and c<d.

blocks.text: For continuous variables, differentiating the CDF gives the pdf: f(x,y)=∂²F/(∂x∂y) at points where the derivative exists. The CDF stores all joint information in one function.

Let U=g(X,Y) and V=h(X,Y). Suppose the map from (x,y) to (u,v) is one-to-one and differentiable. Solve for x=x(u,v) and y=y(u,v). The Jacobian is J=∂(u,v)/∂(x,y), the determinant of the 2×2 matrix of partial derivatives. Then f_{UV}(u,v)=f_{XY}(x,y)/|J|, with x,y replaced by their formulas in u,v. If the map is not one-to-one, split into pieces and add the pieces.

blocks.where: J is the Jacobian; u and v are the new variables; x and y are the old variables.

items: Write u=g(x,y), v=h(x,y) and solve for x,y in terms of u,v.
Compute the four partial derivatives and the determinant J.
Take the absolute value |J|. If J=0 at a point, treat that point separately.
Substitute x(u,v), y(u,v) into f_XY and divide by |J|.
Check that the result integrates to 1 over the image region.

blocks.text: Example: U=X+Y and V=X-Y. Then x=(u+v)/2 and y=(u-v)/2. The derivatives give J=-2, so |J|=2. Hence f_{UV}(u,v)=½ f_{XY}((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2).

spec.title: Joint pmf p(x,y) for two rolls of a die
spec.aria: A three by three table of joint probabilities for the counts of 1s and 2s in two die rolls, with the cell for one 1 and one 2 picked out.

examples.question: A fair die is rolled twice. X = number of 1s, Y = number of 2s. (a) Find P(X=1,Y=1). (b) Find P(X+Y≥1).
steps: There are 6×6=36 ordered outcomes, each with probability 1/36.
For X=1 and Y=1, the two rolls must be (1,2) or (2,1). That is 2 outcomes. So p(1,1)=2/36=1/18≈0.0556.
For X=0 and Y=0, every roll must be 3, 4, 5 or 6. Each roll has 4 choices, so there are 4×4=16 outcomes. p(0,0)=16/36=4/9≈0.4444.
examples.check:
p00 = 16/36
p11 = 2/36
p_ge = 1 - p00
print(round(p11, 4))
print(round(p_ge, 4))

traps: A joint pdf value f(x,y) is not a probability. It can exceed 1. Only a double integral over an area gives probability.
Do not use a rectangle when the region is a triangle. Read the inner and outer limits from the picture.
In the Jacobian formula use |J| with J=∂(u,v)/∂(x,y). If you compute the inverse Jacobian ∂(x,y)/∂(u,v), multiply by it, do not divide.
In the rectangle CDF formula, the signs are + - - +. A sign slip changes the probability.
The joint is not the product of marginals unless the variables are independent. That product is a special case, not the definition.

quiz.q: Define the joint pmf of two discrete variables X and Y and state its two properties.
Why is f(0.5,0.5)=1.4 not impossible for a joint pdf?
quiz.a: A pdf is a density. Values above 1 are allowed; probability comes only from a double integral over an area.

quiz.q: Why is F(x,y) non-decreasing in x?
quiz.a: Increasing x adds more outcomes to the event {X≤x,Y≤y}, so its probability cannot fall.

quiz.q: Using the die-roll joint pmf, find P(X=0,Y=1).
quiz.a: Exactly one 2 and no 1. Choose the 2-roll in 2 ways; the other roll is 3,4,5,6: 4 ways. Favorable=8, total=36, so 8/36=2/9≈0.2222.

quiz.q: For f(x,y)=2 on triangle 0≤y≤x≤1, find P(X+Y≤1).
quiz.a: The part of the triangle with x+y≤1 has area 1/4. Since f=2, probability=2×1/4=1/2.

quiz.q: For U=X+Y, V=X-Y, find J and f_UV.
Explain why P(X=0.3,Y=0.7)=0 for a continuous joint distribution, yet f(0.3,0.7) may be positive.
quiz.a: A single point has area zero, so its double integral is zero. The pdf is a density per unit area, not a point probability.

beyond: Not for the exam. Joint distributions drive insurance and finance: two risks are modelled together so bad days are not assumed independent. In machine learning, a bivariate normal or copula models two correlated features. In wireless networks, joint distributions of signal and interference set outage probabilities. Search next: copula, bivariate normal, Jacobian transformation, joint survival function.
